public_rationale: The claim says the field is 'starting to' realize that scaling alone will not reach AGI. This needs a visible, growing view, not a consensus. Evidence from 2025 shows such a view. On 14 March 2025, The Decoder reported an AAAI survey in which 76% of respondents said scaling existing AI systems was 'unlikely' or 'very unlikely' to produce AGI (e1). On 25 November 2025, Ilya Sutskever said he did not think 100x more scale would transform everything, and that 'it's back to the age of research again' (e2). On 20 November 2025, NeurIPS announced that Turing Award winner Richard Sutton would give an invited talk on 3 December arguing that AI 'has lost its way' and needs agents that learn continually (e3). On 18 November 2025, Oriol Vinyals of Google DeepMind disagreed, saying Gemini 3 showed 'no walls in sight' (e4). In the same post, he described the view that scaling is over as a 'popular belief' (e4). So views were not unanimous, but by the claim's December 2025 date, the view it describes was widely voiced.
limitations: No earlier survey is available for comparison, so the growth of this view is inferred rather than measured.
The AAAI survey sample may not reflect views inside frontier labs.
The NeurIPS item (e3) is a pre-conference announcement of Sutton's talk. It does not record what he said on the day.
The evidence covers views about scaling. It does not show whether scaling can or cannot reach AGI.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI field is now starting to realize that scaling alone will not reach AGI.

statement.excerpt: And now, at last, the field is starting to realize it.
statement.document_title: “Scale Is All You Need” is dead

from_speaker: it = scaling would not get us to AGI
our_interpretation: Plain reading: by late 2025, a growing share of AI researchers, including prominent figures, publicly said that scaling current LLM approaches alone would not reach AGI.
Target period: 2025 up to the post date, the most recent period public evidence covers. 'Starting to' needs only a visible and growing trend, not consensus.
criteria.support_condition: Surveys or prominent researcher statements from 2025 show substantial or growing acceptance that scaling alone will not reach AGI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that in 2025 most researchers and leading figures still held that scaling alone would reach AGI, with no visible shift.

evidence.excerpt: The study found that 76 percent of respondents rated this possibility as "unlikely" or "very unlikely."
evidence.explanation: A survey of 475 AAAI community members found that 76% thought scaling current systems was unlikely to produce AGI.

evidence.excerpt: But is the belief that if you just 100x the scale, everything would be transformed? I don’t think that’s true. So it’s back to the age of research again, just with big computers.
evidence.explanation: A leading figure of the scaling era publicly said scaling alone would not transform things. That is a clear sign of the shift Marcus describes.

evidence.excerpt: Richard Sutton, recipient of the 2024 Turing Award, will argue that as “AI has become a huge industry, to an extent it has lost its way,” and proposes a return to fundamental principles
evidence.explanation: The field's biggest conference gave a keynote slot to a Turing Award winner arguing that the field has lost its way and needs new approaches.

evidence.excerpt: Contra the popular belief that scaling is over—which we discussed in our NeurIPS '25 talk with @ilyasut and @quocleix—the team delivered a drastic jump.
evidence.publisher: Oriol Vinyals (Google DeepMind) on X, via Thread Reader
evidence.explanation: Shows that some frontier-lab leaders still pushed back on limits to scaling. It also confirms that the 'scaling is over' view had become a 'popular belief'.
